title: Composite RICE + LCI (Latent Cost Impact) prioritization framework and runbook for roadmap cycles
creator: Sana Iyer
body:
Summary: Propose and operationalize a Composite RICE + LCI framework that augments classic RICE (Reach, Impact, Confidence, Effort) with a Latent Cost Impact (LCI) multiplier that captures expected long-term inference dollar and latency footprint. Goal: make roadmap scoring reflect not only product value but also measurable production economics for Redwood Inference (token cost, throughput pressure, and SLO risk).

Motivation: Existing RICE scores in our roadmap often prioritize high-user-value features without sufficiently accounting for recurring per-token costs, expected average latency degradation under load, or the operational complexity of long-lived model variants. This leads to surprises during Dedicated and Private rollouts where unit economics matter. This framework aims to be pragmatic, repeatable, and automatable in the roadmap cadence.

Core idea: Keep R, I, C, E as the base numeric inputs (0-10 normalized); compute classic RICE = (R * I * C) / E. Then compute LCI as a separate normalized multiplier that penalizes initiatives with high expected token cost, negative latency delta, or high operational churn. Final CompositeScore = RICE / LCI (where LCI >= 0.5; higher LCI => worse economics => reduces score). LCI is computed from three signals: Estimated incremental per-month token cost (normalized), Expected P50/P95 latency delta under projected qps (normalized), and Operational churn factor (deployments / rollbacks / model variants).

Deliverables: 1) Scoring spreadsheet and formula sheet; 2) Implementation in roadmap scoring tool (CSV import + computed columns); 3) Short runbook for PMs to estimate inputs; 4) Pilot scoring of 12 candidate initiatives for Q2 planning; 5) Dashboard showing how composite score shifts decisions vs classic RICE.

Why different from previous work: Many existing docs focus on RICE alone or cost-weighted heuristics. This deliverable explicitly binds token-unit economics and latency SLO risk to prioritization with a defensible normalization strategy and an operational runbook for PMs and Eng to estimate inputs consistently.

Attachments / artifacts: linking to plan doc (Confluence) and example spreadsheet in Drive will be added in follow-ups.
acceptance_criteria: Framework documented with formulas and normalization steps in the Confluence page
Roadmap scoring sheet (CSV + computed columns) produced and validated with sample initiatives
PM runbook (2-page) published describing how to estimate Reach, Impact, Confidence, Effort, token-cost, latency delta, operational churn
Scoring tool updated to compute CompositeScore automatically for CSV imports
Pilot: 12 initiatives scored and reviewed with Eng + Design; recommended top-6 by CompositeScore annotated with tradeoffs
Stakeholder alignment: GTM/Revenue, Platform, and SRE sign-offs on LCI assumptions
steps: Draft formula and normalization bands for token-cost, latency delta, and operational churn (Owner: PM)
Work session with Serving runtime (Eng) to define realistic latency delta buckets for projected qps (Owner: Liam)
Produce scoring spreadsheet and pre-fill 12 candidate initiatives (Owner: PM team)
Eng review: confirm assumptions and provide cost multipliers / per-token estimates (Owner: ENG ops)
Iterate runbook language to minimize ambiguity (Owner: Design + PM)
Push minor update to roadmap scoring tool to accept LCI inputs and compute CompositeScore (Owner: Data/Analytics)
Pilot review meeting and decision log (Owner: PM lead)
Document retrospective notes after Q2 planning (Owner: PM)
If pilot successful, roll out framework to quarterly cycle and embed into OKR intake flows
risks: LCI inputs may be noisy early and could bias against high-value features that transiently increase cost
PMs may consistently over/underestimate token costs without quick feedback loops
Work required to integrate estimated per-token cost signals from billing/usage may be nontrivial
A too-aggressive LCI multiplier could starve platform investments that reduce long-term costs
Stakeholder pushback from revenue/GTM if high-revenue features are deprioritized by economics
tradeoffs: Conservative LCI reduces chance of starving high revenue features but blunts economic signal
Aggressive LCI surfaces cost risks early but requires a strong review guardrail to avoid false negatives
Manual estimation reduces engineering work but increases variance; automated signals are more accurate but require infra effort
Keep framework lightweight for adoption vs. build a heavyweight model for precision
sample_scoring_examples: Example initiative A: User-facing streaming chat - R=8 I=9 C=7 E=5 => RICE=100.8 (normalized) ; Token-cost bucket=high (LCI_component=1.6), Latency bucket=small (1.1), Churn=low (1.0) => LCI=1.43 => CompositeScore~70.6 => moves down relative to raw RICE

Example initiative B: Batching / KV cache improvement - R=4 I=6 C=8 E=3 => RICE=64.0 ; Token-cost bucket=low (0.8), Latency bucket=improve (0.7), Churn=medium (1.1) => LCI=0.87 => CompositeScore~73.6 => moves up (shows platform investments can outrank some feature work)

Notes on normalization: we map raw cost deltas to buckets (low=0.7, medium=1.0, high=1.6). Latency improvements map below 1.0, degradations above 1.0. Churn is 0.9-1.4 depending on expected number of variants/rollouts
comments: 2026-02-12 Sana Iyer: initial draft completed, requesting Eng validation on latency buckets and realistic cost multipliers. Added sample lines for two initiatives.

2026-02-18 Marco Ruiz (Eng): reviewed latency bucket definitions; suggested adding separate P50 vs P95 considerations and using P95 as primary risk signal. Suggested LCI weight 0.6*P95 + 0.3*tokenCost + 0.1*churn.

2026-02-22 Clara Nguyen (SRE): asked for linkage to billing telemetry. We should map token-cost estimates to historical per-model per-token averages in billing dataset. Action: ENG-48211 will expose model-level per-token cost export.
2026-02-25 Design review (Priya Rao): runbook needs a short decision-flow diagram and examples for non-technical PMs. Assigned PRD update to DES-1422.
2026-03-01 Liam O'Connor: updated scoring sheet with 12 pilot initiatives; scheduled pilot review on 2026-03-05. Added acceptance criteria and pilot deliverables.

2026-03-02 Revenue (Alicia Monroe): flagged that certain GTM experiments produce long-term revenue channel effects that are hard to quantify by R/I alone; recommended we add an override tag 'strategic-revenue' that triggers cross-functional review rather than an automatic score bump
next_steps: Finalize normalization formula (incorporate Marco's P95 suggestion) and publish Confluence page (owner: Sana)
ENG: expose model-level per-token cost telemetry endpoint (ENG-48211) for automated LCI population
Data: add CompositeScore computation to scoring import pipeline and enable CSV preview in the tool (owner: Data)
Run pilot review meeting on 2026-03-05 and capture decision log
If pilot passes acceptance criteria, adopt CompositeScore as tiebreaker in Q2 planning and update OKR intake template
